adversarial_test_results.prompt: Thomas Hardy published his final novel in 1895 and spent the remaining years of his life writing poetry at Max Gate, the house he had designed himself on the edge of Dorchester. The garden pleased him more than the house. He planted trees along the drive and complained when the roots disturbed the lawn. In the evenings he read aloud from the Bible or from the poems of William Barnes, whose Dorset dialect he admired. After his death in 1928 his heart was buried beside Florence in Stinsford churchyard, while his ashes were placed in Poets' Corner at Westminster Abbey. The divided burial has puzzled biographers ever since, though the family insisted it was his own wish.
